name: Nicaragua
summary: Blue, white and blue horizontal bands with the coat of arms: a triangle with five volcanoes, a Phrygian cap and a rainbow, encircled by 'República de Nicaragua — América Central'. It is one of the few national flags to include the colour purple, in the rainbow.
origin: The design follows the flag of the Federal Republic of Central America (1823–1841). Nicaragua adopted it on 4 September 1908, and the specifications were set by law on 27 August 1971.

colors.name: Blue
colors.meaning: The two oceans bordering the country; also justice and loyalty.

colors.name: White
colors.meaning: The land between the oceans; also peace and purity.

symbols.name: Triangle with five volcanoes
symbols.description: An equilateral triangle with five green volcanoes between two seas.
symbols.meaning: Equality; the volcanoes represent the five former members of the Central American federation.

symbols.name: Rainbow
symbols.description: A rainbow across the top of the triangle, including purple.

facts: Its rainbow makes it one of only two national flags with purple, along with Dominica's.
El Salvador's flag is very similar, with a different emblem.
The Sandinista movement uses a red and black flag, flown alongside the national flag.
clues: Blue, white and blue bands with a triangle of five volcanoes under a rainbow.
Its rainbow makes it one of only two national flags with purple.
Its emblem names its country and 'América Central'.
